geographical_area: City of Milan and its urban speech community (classical and contemporary Milanese). Hinterland Lombard varieties (Brianza, Comasco, Varesotto, Lodigiano, Ticinese) and Eastern Lombard (Bergamasco, mode pota) are not covered.
linguistic_classification: Western Lombard (Gallo-Italic), Milanese; unstandardised, with a long literary tradition (Maggi, Porta, Cherubini).
language_family: Indo-European > Romance > Gallo-Italic > Lombard > Western Lombard (Milanese)
orthographic_conventions: Default: contemporary urban Milanese in modern spelling (ö for the front rounded vowel, ü for /y/). Classical Cherubini/Porta orthography (oeu, u for /y/) is reference only, on request, never mixed in. Common to both: doubled vowels for length (andaa, hoo, voo), doubled consonants for short stressed vowels, final vowels dropped except -a, infinitives without -r (andà, vedè, vess), ch/gh before e/i, apostrophes for elision (l'è, gh'è). Classical oeu/u spelling is documented as reference and not mixed in.
description_en: Milanese of Milan: subject clitics (mi a, te, el/la, i), post-verbal negation with minga, compound perfect with avè/vess + participle (no passato remoto), progressive with son dree a + infinitive, gh'è for existence, avè present hoo/hé/hà/hèmm/avìi/hann, and a dry, ironic voice with mock-absurd dismissals (va scuà 'l mar). Mode word: pirla.
description_it: Milanese di Milano: clitici soggetto (mi a, te, el/la, i), negazione posposta con minga, passato prossimo con avè/vess + participio (niente passato remoto), progressivo con son dree a + infinito, gh'è per l'esistenza, presente di avè hoo/hé/hà/hèmm/avìi/hann e una voce asciutta e ironica con congedi assurdi (va scuà 'l mar). Parola identificativa: pirla.

identifier_word.meaning_en: Northern/Milanese vulgar word for 'idiot, jerk' (also a vulgar word for penis); the source-attested Milanese phrase is Te se propri un pirla!
identifier_word.meaning_it: Voce settentrionale/milanese volgare per 'sciocco, imbecille' (anche 'pene'); la frase milanese attestata è Te se propri un pirla!
identifier_word.attestation: Wiktionary (Italian entry) records pirla as regional, vulgar, 'fool, idiot' and 'penis', probably related to pirlare; MilanoFree lists Te se propri un pirla! among Milanese insults and elon.io calls it a vulgar Milanese term now fairly mild. The mode name is an Italian-regional spelling of a Milanese-origin word, not the academic name of the variety. No scholarly etymology was read; the 'spinning top' origin is plausible but unverified.

known_limitations: No native-speaker review: all example sentences are AI-illustrative.

Open linguistic documentation of Milanese is thin. Grammar rests on Wikipedia/Wiktionary and low-reliability popular pages; the full present of vess (semm, sii, hinn) and several verb forms are general knowledge, flagged unverified in the profile.
Source spellings are inconsistent (classical oeu/u mixed with modern ü/ö and ad-hoc accents); proverbs keep the spelling of the page they came from.
The brief's 'interrogative inversion' is documented only as archaic (Voeurela? / Cantel?); modern Milanese keeps the clitic before the verb, so the profile does not use inversion.
No Milanese-specific blasphemies were documented, so none are generated; level 5 is reached only by stacking documented level 3-4 items.
Profanity items come from popular web pages (low reliability) and are marked unverified; lògia and terun are documented for recognition only (generation_allowed false).
The mode word pirla is pan-northern Italian slang as well as Milanese; the catalog aliases pirlòn/pirlone were not found in any source read.
